text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Tuesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

-- The council of Tauras Bank fired bank board chairman and administration head Gintaras Terleckas, his assistant Rasa Shereniene and finance director Valdas Vitkunas. An extraordinary meeting of shareholders is expected in the near future, which may discuss the devaluation of the bank's shares. Experts from the Bank of Lithuania are investigating Tauras Bank but have not reached any conclusions.

-- Mazheikiu Nafta expects to receive $50 million worth of long-term loans from Western banks for the construction of petrol stations. The company expects to borrow another $105 million at the beginning of next year for the reconstruction of its processing factory.

-- Parliament Chairman Vytautas Landsbergis will go to the U.S. on Wednesday where he will participate in events to mark the anniversary of the Martynas Mazhvydas Catechism, Lithuania's first book, at the Library of Congress in Washington.
-- For the first five months of this year, imports of beef decreased by 103 tonnes and imports of pork by 130 tonnes.
-- President Algirdas Brazauskas met with MPs but gave no hints whether he would sign into law legislation, passed earlier this month, on the restitution of property.
-- Landsbergis said a package of Western-style anti-corruption laws to regulate income declaration and the conflict of interest was being prepared.

-- Central bank governor Reinoldijus Sharkinas denied that a 17 million ECU European Union loan, taken by the government of former prime minister Adolfas Shlezevichius, was lost in troubled Tauras Bank.
